files.workings: 4000 frames at 8000 Hz is 0.5 s; (120 x 4000 + 8000) / 16000 = 30.5, floor 30. A LIST/INFO chunk with an odd-sized ISFT item precedes the data.
4000 data bytes / block align 2 = 2000 frames; (120 x 2000 + 8000) / 16000 = 15.5, floor 15.
1600 data bytes / block align 4 = 400 frames; (120 x 400 + 8000) / 16000 = 3.5, floor 3.
200 frames at 8000 Hz is exactly 1.5 ticks; (120 x 200 + 8000) / 16000 = 2.0, so a half tick rounds up to 2.
one frame; (120 + 8000) / 16000 = 0.5075, floor 0, raised to the minimum of 1. The odd data chunk is padded.
block align 256 holds (256 - 7) x 2 + 2 = 500 samples; 4 blocks and no fact chunk = 2000 frames; (120 x 2000 + 8000) / 16000 = 15.5, floor 15.
the same four 500-sample blocks, but the fact chunk says 1900 frames and wins; (120 x 1900 + 8000) / 16000 = 14.75, floor 14.
block align 256 holds (256 - 4) x 2 + 1 = 505 samples; 4 blocks = 2020 frames (fact 2020); (120 x 2020 + 8000) / 16000 = 15.65, floor 15.

stereo block align 512 is two 4-byte channel headers then 63 groups of 8 bytes (4 per channel): 504 samples per channel plus the header sample = 505 frames per block; 2 blocks and no fact chunk = 1010 frames; (120 x 1010 + 8000) / 16000 = 8.075, floor 8.

a GM System On sysex, then 96 ticks at the default 500000, a tempo change to 250000 at tick 96, then 192 ticks at 250000 to the end at 288; N = 96 x 500000 + 192 x 250000 = 96000000; (12 x 96000000 + 100000 x 96) / (200000 x 96) = 60.5, floor 60 (1 s).

two tracks merged by absolute tick: default 500000 for ticks 0-120, 400000 for 120-360 (tempo track), 1000000 for 360-720; the note track ends last at 720, so the tempo carries on past its own end at 480. N = 120 x 500000 + 240 x 400000 + 360 x 1000000 = 516000000; (12 x 516000000 + 100000 x 240) / (200000 x 240) = 129.5, floor 129 (2.15 s).
no note events: the tempo map alone gives the length. 480 ticks at 500000 then 480 at 250000; N = 360000000 = 0.75 s; (12 x 360000000 + 100000 x 480) / (200000 x 480) = 45.5, floor 45.
only an end-of-track at tick 0; N = 0; (0 + 100000 x 480) / (200000 x 480) = 0.5, floor 0, raised to the minimum of 1.

an XG System On sysex (manufacturer 43, model 4C) and controller 0 set to 1; ends at 480; N = 240000000 = 0.5 s; (12 x 240000000 + 100000 x 480) / (200000 x 480) = 30.5, floor 30. Dialect xg, bank select true.
a GS Reset sysex (manufacturer 41, model 42), no bank select; ends at 96; N = 48000000 = 0.5 s; (12 x 48000000 + 100000 x 96) / (200000 x 96) = 30.5, floor 30. Dialect gs, bank select false.

proposed.P-1: Row sampling: the row for tick t is the state at the end of the audio phase of tick t, before time advances; a voice started in tick t has position 0 in row t.
proposed.P-2: Cue tick: the tick at which the applier applied the transition. Effects drained when the applier registers carry the registration tick and follow the start soundfont.set; a one-shot's finish emits media.stop in the audio phase of its end tick.
proposed.P-3: Finish: at the audio phase of its end tick a one-shot is removed from the track (the track keeps file and flags), a finished fact is recorded once, and the track's primary view then reads position 0 and an unknown length.
proposed.P-4: A paused voice keeps its pre-pause startTick, endTick and fade start; resume shifts all three by the paused span, and a fade started while paused begins counting at resume.
proposed.P-5: Loop is per voice (the voice rows carry it); a track's flags are the loop bit of its voice 0 only (the wait and restart requests are play-time instructions and are not retained); a track's file is the file most recently started on it.
proposed.P-6: Fades: the descriptor is cleared in the audio phase of the tick at which the elapsed ticks reach the duration and the volume becomes the target; a zero-duration fade is a media.fade cue with durationTicks 0 and an immediate set; mediaVolume cancels a running fade; a fade with no voice argument is a track (bus) fade, kept beside the track and not in a voice's fade field.
proposed.P-7: Cue fields: media.play carries loop, flags (the loop bit), the starting positionTicks (the synced position for a synced start) and the voice's script volume; stop, pause, resume, seek, flags and fade carry the track and voice index (a bus fade or volume has voice null, the master volume has track null).
proposed.P-8: Waits: a finite one-shot's wait reads the voice's current endTick (so a pause or a seek moves it); a pass wait wakes when the voice's pass index exceeds the index at creation; a wait whose voice is gone (stopped, finished, stolen, or replaced so the cue id differs) wakes at the next waits phase.
proposed.P-9: Load: the cue counter is the larger of the current and the saved one; the current configured tracks, voice counts and bank stay unchanged and unconfigured saved tracks/slots are ignored (MEDIA-4/audio-save-load, #481). Re-emit the current effective bank first; a resumed non-music voice's cue has tick = load tick minus its saved position and position 0, music's has the load tick and position 0; saving a voice with a running fade, loading a paused voice and loading with a thread parked in a wait are outside the oracle (a hard error).
proposed.P-10: A same-file play on a single-voice track while playing is a recorded no-cue outcome (carry-on on music, ignored elsewhere); with a restart request it is stop then play; on a paused single-voice track it is unruled.
proposed.P-11: Legacy names resolve case-insensitively to media/<lower-case name>; each is evaluated as the standard call of 6.2's mapping table and records a legacy fact naming it.
proposed.P-12: Video: playavi stops the music at the call tick (a media.stop only when a voice exists) and parks the thread; video.ended is stamped at the held tick, the row of the next consumed tick, whose waits phase wakes the thread and then posts a restart music.play (source video, retained file and loop flag, restart set) when the music track retained a file.
proposed.P-13: Steal: the victim is the lowest priority, then the oldest startTick, then the lowest index (a paused voice counts as active with its stale start); the stolen index is stopped (media.stop) before the new play; a steal fact names the victim.
proposed.P-14: A file no decoder accepts plays with length null and endTick null and raises one media.asset-format diagnostic at the play; a seek or a wait on an unknown length raises media.asset-length; a sync on an unknown-length destination raises media.sync-source and starts the otherwise valid destination at position zero.
proposed.P-15: Scripts give seconds as whole milliseconds; ticks = floor((ms x 60 + 500) / 1000), the exact integer form of floor(seconds x 60 + 1/2).
proposed.P-16: Late runner: for a media.play the runner facts apply, in this order, the drop (finite, not looping, not music, lateness at least 15 ticks), then the loop modulo, then not starting a finite one-shot whose caught-up position reaches its length.
proposed.P-17: Diagnostic choice where 6.2 lists several: a voice index at or above the configured count, or a voice with no occupant for a seek, fade or volume, is media.unknown-voice.
proposed.P-18: A row lists the track (bus) volume or an active track fade only for tracks not at 100, the master volume only when not 100, and the script bank when set; none of them is read by a load.

corpus.note: Lengths are measured by tools/fixtures/audio/length.mjs, not by the core decoders; entry 6.5 must agree with them. The files are read only when fetched and are never committed.
